messages.author: e4c21733ed33c566
messages.subject: Return ui & vi (correlated & uncorrelated heterogeneity)
parts:
Hi, I'm fairly new to R & R inla and I was wondering if there is a function that would return the random effects ui (for modeling spatial residual variation) and vi (for modeling unstructured noise) for all n rows in my data. 

Here are the spatial parameters i'm using

formula <- y ~ 1 + f(ID, model="bym",graph=CIN.adj, scale.model=TRUE,
                    hyper=list(prec.unstruct=list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.001)), prec.spatial=list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.001))))


mod.od <- inla(formula,family="poisson",
                      data=data.overdoses,E=E,
                      control.compute=list(dic=TRUE))

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Return ui & vi (correlated & uncorrelated heterogeneity)
parts:
Hi,

if you look at

inla.doc("bym")

then the bym model is defined as the spatial one, u, and u+v, so
its kind of hard(er) to extract both u and v. you may just use the sum
of two models, like done in

demo(Bym)

for which each of the term is fully given in the output

H
